approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that would create a national framework for reducing air pollution from certain products.

The package would let the minister designate products as emissions-controlled, set rules for certifying them to meet emissions standards, and create offences for importing or supplying uncertified products.
The first products expected to be covered are new non-road spark ignition engines and equipment, including marine engines and small engines up to 19 kilowatts.
Sets up a national scheme for emissions standards on certain products.
Allows the minister to prescribe products and make rules for certification and exemptions.
Creates offences and penalties for importing or supplying uncertified emissions-controlled products.
Establishes a charge on imports and domestic manufacture of emissions-controlled products to recover costs.
Importers, domestic manufacturers, and suppliers of non-road spark ignition engines and equipment.

The Product Emissions Standards (Excise) Charges Bill 2017 imposes a charge on domestically manufactured products prescribed under product emissions standards legislation, enabling full cost recovery of regulatory costs alongside companion bills.

The Product Emissions Standards (Customs) Charges Bill 2017 imposes a charge on importing products prescribed under product emissions standards legislation, enabling full cost recovery of regulation costs alongside the Excise Charges Bill and the Product Emissions Standards Bill 2017.

The speaker moved that the Product Emissions Standards Bill 2017, the Product Emissions Standards (Excise) Charges Bill 2017, the Product Emissions Standards (Customs) Charges Bill 2017, and the Product Emissions Standards (Consequential Provisions) Bill be referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.
